sources.title: Berger, Singer, Bliss, Moring 2011, Ni-Co laterite deposits of the world: database and grade and tonnage models (USGS OFR 2011-1058)
Mosier, Singer, Moring, Galloway 2012, Podiform chromite deposits: database and grade and tonnage models (USGS SIR 2012-5157)
U.S. Geological Survey 2025, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025 (iron ore, manganese, chromium, nickel, titanium mineral concentrates, vanadium, platinum-group metals, bauxite)

Earth iron-ferro compilation of well-known published endowment figures (production + reserves + resources) from company reports, national geological surveys and review papers named in each entry's ref; positions and outlines from published maps
sources.licence: facts with citation (no third-party data copied); compilation CC0 by the Earth project

deposits.name: Kiirunavaara (Kiruna)
deposits.ref: about 950 Mt mined by 2013 said to be one third of the resource (mining-technology.com); ore body 4 km x 80 m average dipping 60 E to at least 2 km

deposits.name: Malmberget
deposits.ref: LKAB; about 20 magnetite-hematite ore bodies over 5 x 2.5 km

deposits.name: Grangesberg
deposits.ref: mined 1550s-1989 about 150 Mt; remaining resource about 115 Mt at 40 % Fe (Grangesberg Iron)

deposits.name: Sydvaranger (Bjornevatn)
deposits.ref: banded magnetite quartzite; Sydvaranger resource statements

deposits.name: Dunderland (Rana)
deposits.ref: Rana Gruber; Neoproterozoic-Cambrian iron formation in Caledonian nappes

deposits.name: Magnitnaya Gora (Magnitogorsk)
deposits.ref: Carboniferous skarn magnetite; worked out by 1990s

deposits.name: Bakal
deposits.ref: Riphean siderite with limonite cap (siderite has no game ore; limonite is its weathering product)

deposits.name: Sokolov-Sarbai and Kachar (Rudny)
deposits.ref: Turgai skarn-magnetite belt (Sokolov Sarbai Kachar Kurzhunkul); ERG

deposits.name: Kerch ironstone
deposits.ref: Pliocene oolitic brown iron ore (Kerch basin)

deposits.name: Erzberg
deposits.ref: siderite-ankerite in Devonian limestone; >230 Mt mined since antiquity (VA Erzberg)

deposits.name: Huttenberg
deposits.ref: Noric siderite; worked since the Iron Age

deposits.name: Bilbao (Somorrostro)
deposits.ref: Cretaceous replacement siderite with rubio hematite; about 200 Mt mined 1850-1990

deposits.name: Elba (Rio Marina-Calamita)
deposits.ref: Etruscan to 1981; Miocene-Pliocene skarn and replacement hematite

deposits.name: Hajigak
deposits.ref: Afghan Geological Survey and BGS: about 1.8 Gt at 62 % Fe (1960s estimate in the Russian classification); 16 ore bodies up to 3 km long along 9 km

deposits.name: Bayan Obo
deposits.ref: Fe-REE-Nb (iron ore resource about 1.5 Gt); fluorite (about 10 % of the ore) is a share here

deposits.name: Simandou (blocks 1-4)
deposits.ref: Rio Tinto and WCS resource statements

deposits.name: Zanaga
deposits.ref: Zanaga Iron Ore Co JORC resource 6.9 Gt at 32 % Fe over 25 of 47 km strike (reserve 2.07 Gt at 33.9 %); itabirite with a hematite cap

deposits.name: Wadi Shatti ironstone
deposits.ref: US Bureau of Mines Minerals Yearbook 1973: 3.6 Gt in three oolitic horizons (over half at 50 % Fe; rest 40-50 %); USGS cites 795 Mt at 52 % for the best part

deposits.name: Sishen
deposits.ref: Kumba Iron Ore; Paleoproterozoic BIF-hosted hematite

deposits.name: Mining Area C and South Flank
Robe Valley channel iron (Mesa J-Mesa A)
Solomon (Firetail-Kings)
deposits.ref: Fortescue; channel iron and Brockman detrital

deposits.name: Wabana (Bell Island)
deposits.ref: Ordovician oolitic hematite; extends under Conception Bay

deposits.name: Pea Ridge
deposits.ref: Mesoproterozoic iron oxide-apatite under Paleozoic cover

deposits.name: El Laco
deposits.ref: Andes Iron/CAP resource 734 Mt at 49 % Fe; Pliocene magnetite flows

deposits.name: El Mutun
deposits.ref: Sergeotecmin 2006: 40.2 Gt of iron ore at about 50 % Fe; Neoproterozoic Jacadigo-type banded iron formation

deposits.name: Urucum-Corumba
deposits.ref: Jacadigo Group iron formation (Mn beds listed separately)

deposits.name: Mesabi Range natural ores
deposits.ref: about 2.5 Gt of direct-shipping ore mined 1892-1980s from the Biwabik Iron Formation

deposits.name: Groote Eylandt
deposits.ref: GEMCO; Cretaceous pisolitic oxide ore (rhodochrosite is the game's Mn ore)

deposits.name: Moanda (Bangombe)
deposits.ref: COMILOG; supergene oxide ore on Francevillian Mn protore

deposits.name: Nsuta
deposits.ref: Birimian Mn carbonate with oxide cap

deposits.name: Urucum manganese
deposits.ref: Mn beds in Jacadigo iron formation

deposits.name: Bolshoi Tokmak
deposits.ref: Oligocene Mn carbonate (largest European Mn resource)

deposits.name: Tongren-Songtao Datangpo manganese (Pujue-Gaodi-Daotuo-Taoziping)
deposits.ref: Guizhou government 2019 (via SMM news): Pujue 203 + Gaodi 161 + Daotuo 142 + Taoziping 106 Mt; Neoproterozoic Datangpo Formation rhodochrosite ore at about 20 % Mn mostly 500-1400 m deep

deposits.name: Sukinda
deposits.ref: Sukinda Valley ultramafic complex (about 95 % of India's chromite)

deposits.name: Talnakh-Oktyabrsky-Kharaelakh
deposits.ref: Nornickel 2024: Norilsk Division proved and probable reserves 1203 Mt at 0.71 % Ni 1.31 % Cu 4.52 g/t PGM; plus resources and about 80 years of production; flat sill-hosted disseminated and massive ore

deposits.name: Sudbury South Range West (Creighton-Copper Cliff)
deposits.ref: Sudbury total endowment about 1.65 Gt at 1.2 % Ni and 1.1 % Cu (Lightfoot 2017)

deposits.name: Sudbury North Range (Levack-Coleman-Strathcona)
deposits.ref: North Range contact and footwall ores

deposits.name: Voisey's Bay
deposits.ref: Vale resource 141 Mt at 1.6 % Ni (Ovoid 32 Mt at 2.8 % Ni)

deposits.name: Kambalda dome
deposits.ref: about 1.2 Mt Ni produced from komatiite contact ores

deposits.name: Duluth Complex (Babbitt-NorthMet)
deposits.ref: low-grade Cu-Ni-PGE along the basal contact

deposits.name: Tellnes
deposits.ref: Titania AS; ilmenite norite dyke 2.7 km x 400 m

deposits.name: Lac Tio (Allard Lake)
deposits.ref: Rio Tinto Fer et Titane; hemo-ilmenite in anorthosite (Allard Lake)

deposits.name: Panzhihua
deposits.ref: Panxi V-Ti magnetite (ore about 33 % Fe 11 % TiO2 0.3 % V2O5); vanadinite stands for the V in magnetite

deposits.name: Suwalki (Krzemianka-Udryn)
deposits.ref: Fe-Ti-V ores in anorthosite under 850 m of cover (PGI)

deposits.name: Kachkanar (Gusevogorsk)
deposits.ref: EVRAZ KGOK low-grade titanomagnetite clinopyroxenite (16 % Fe)

deposits.name: Stillwater J-M Reef
deposits.ref: Sibanye-Stillwater; J-M Reef about 40 km by 1-3 m

deposits.name: Norilsk-1 disseminated ore
deposits.ref: Nornickel 2022: 39 Mt reserves at 4.71 g/t PGM 0.25 % Ni left after about 80 years of open-pit and underground mining

deposits.name: Iss and Tura PGE placers
deposits.ref: Ural platinum placers worked from 1824 (about 300 t Pt from the Urals)

deposits.name: Nizhny Tagil PGE placers
deposits.ref: placers from the Nizhny Tagil dunite massif

deposits.name: Kondyor placers
deposits.ref: placers of the Kondyor ring massif

deposits.name: Gongyi-Mianchi (Henan)
deposits.ref: buried Carboniferous diaspore bauxite (bed in Carboniferous)

deposits.name: Conakry laterite iron (Kaloum)
deposits.ref: lateritic iron crust on Kaloum dunite; mined 1953-1966

deposits.name: Moa-Mayari limonite cap
deposits.ref: iron-rich limonite zone of the Mayari-Baracoa laterites (Ni counted in the laterite entries)

deposits.name: Clinton ironstone (Oneida County)
deposits.ref: Silurian Clinton Group oolitic hematite (type area)

deposits.name: Richards Bay dunes (Hillendale-Zulti)
deposits.ref: Richards Bay Minerals coastal dune heavy-mineral sands

deposits.name: Moma (Namalope-Pilivili)
deposits.ref: Kenmare resource (about 3 % heavy minerals mostly ilmenite)

deposits.name: Grande Cote
deposits.ref: Eramet; dune sands about 1.6 % heavy minerals

deposits.name: Kempirsai (Donskoye: Molodezhnoye-40 Years KazSSR-Millionnoye)
deposits.ref: TNK Kazchrome; podiform giant of the Kempirsai ophiolite (world's largest podiform chromite district)

deposits.name: Morowali-Bahodopi laterites
deposits.ref: Indonesian Ni ore resources (MEMR 2023) beyond the 2011 USGS entries

deposits.name: Weda Bay extension (Tanjung Ulie-Santa Monica)
deposits.ref: Eramet-Tsingshan resource beyond the 2011 USGS entry

deposits.name: Kolaka-Pomalaa extension
deposits.ref: ANTAM resources beyond the 2011 USGS entry

areas.name: Hamersley iron province (Brockman and Marra Mamba iron formations)
areas.ref: Geoscience Australia AIMR (iron ore identified resources); Hamersley Group BIF; listed giant hematite and channel-iron deposits excluded; outlines are the iron districts (Chichester Range, Solomon-Eliwana, Brockman-Tom Price-Paraburdoo, West Angelas-Mining Area C-Yandi-Newman-Jimblebar), not the whole province

areas.name: Carajas iron formation (Grao Para Group jaspilites)
areas.ref: Vale resource statements; jaspilite outside the listed Serra Norte, S11D and Serra Leste bodies; outlines are the plateaus (Serra Norte, Serra Sul, Serra Leste)

areas.name: Quadrilatero Ferrifero itabirites (Caue Formation)
areas.ref: DNPM/ANM and Vale resource statements; Itabira listed separately; outlines are the itabirite ridges (Serra do Curral, Serra da Moeda, Serra Azul, Gandarela-Mariana, Ouro Branco)

areas.name: Kryvyi Rih iron basin (Saksagan suite)
areas.ref: Ukrainian state balance (iron quartzites and rich ores); Kremenchuk listed separately

areas.name: Kursk Magnetic Anomaly (Belgorod-Stary Oskol and Mikhailovsky districts)
areas.ref: Russian state balance: about 30 Gt of rich (martite-hematite) ore and ferruginous quartzites under 50-700 m of Phanerozoic cover; outlines are the Stary Oskol-Gubkin, Belgorod (Yakovlevo) and Mikhailovsky districts

areas.name: Mesabi Range taconite (Biwabik Iron Formation)
areas.ref: USGS MCS 2025 (US resources 110 Gt usable ore, mostly Lake Superior taconite); natural ores listed separately

areas.name: Labrador Trough (Sokoman Formation)
areas.ref: Quebec and Newfoundland-Labrador resource compilations; Carol Lake, Mont-Wright and Schefferville listed separately; outlines are the iron districts (Gagnon-Fermont-Wabush, Schefferville-Knob Lake, Lac Otelnuk-Hayot)

areas.name: Singhbhum-Bonai-Keonjhar iron ore group (horseshoe synclinorium)
areas.ref: Indian Bureau of Mines National Mineral Inventory (hematite resources of Odisha and Jharkhand); outlines are the two limbs (Noamundi-Joda-Barbil-Gua, Kiriburu-Bolani-Barsua-Kalta)

areas.name: Lorraine-Luxembourg minette (Aalenian oolitic ironstone)
areas.ref: about 3 Gt mined 1870-1997 from an original resource of about 6 Gt at 28-35 % Fe (BRGM)

areas.name: Cleveland ironstone (Main Seam)
areas.ref: about 300 Mt mined 1850-1964 (BGS); berthierine-siderite oolite, limonite as the game's brown ore

areas.name: Clinton ironstone, Birmingham district (Red Mountain Formation)
areas.ref: about 375 Mt of red ore mined 1870-1971 (Alabama Geological Survey); Silurian oolitic hematite

areas.name: Kalahari manganese field (Hotazel Formation)
areas.ref: about 13.6 Gt of Mn ore (Cairncross and Beukes 2013); USGS MCS 2025: South Africa holds about 70 % of world Mn resources

areas.name: Nikopol manganese basin (Marhanets-Pokrov)
areas.ref: Oligocene oxide-carbonate Mn bed; Ukrainian state balance about 2 Gt

areas.name: Chiatura manganese (Oligocene)
areas.ref: about 140 Mt produced since 1879 plus about 220 Mt reserves (Georgian Manganese)

areas.name: Bushveld Critical Zone chromitites (LG6, MG1-MG4)
areas.ref: USGS MCS 2025: world chromite resources >12 Gt, 95 % in Kazakhstan and southern Africa; the Critical Zone holds about 72 % of the world's chromite ore (Viljoen 2016, Episodes), so about 8.6 Gt

areas.name: Great Dyke chromitite seams
areas.ref: USGS MCS 2025 (Zimbabwe reserves 540 Mt shipping-grade); older estimates give over 10 Gt (Northern Miner); half of that is used for seams 1-11

areas.name: Bushveld Merensky Reef and UG2 chromitite
areas.ref: USGS MCS 2025 (South Africa PGM reserves 63,000 t); Merensky about 5.5 g/t and UG2 about 5 g/t 4E over about 1 m

areas.name: Platreef (Bushveld northern limb)
areas.ref: Anglo American Mogalakwena and Ivanhoe Platreef resource statements (bulk 1.5-3 g/t 4E)

areas.name: Great Dyke Main Sulphide Zone
areas.ref: USGS MCS 2025 (Zimbabwe PGM reserves 1,200 t); MSZ 2-3 m at about 3.5 g/t (Zimplats, Unki, Mimosa)

areas.name: Bushveld Main Magnetite Layer (Upper Zone)
areas.ref: Mapochs and Rhovan V magnetite (1.5-2 % V2O5 over about 2 m); USGS MCS 2025; the vanadinite bed stands for the V-richest base of the layer
